description.summary: **FICTION**: A famous creepypasta from 2010 about Soviet researchers conducting a sleep deprivation experiment on five test subjects in the 1940s. The story is entirely fictional with no historical basis, though often mistaken for real events.
description.full: **THIS IS DOCUMENTED FICTION - NOT A REAL HISTORICAL EVENT**: The Russian Sleep Experiment is one of the most famous creepypastas in internet folklore. The story describes Soviet researchers in the late 1940s testing an experimental gas-based stimulant on five political prisoners, keeping them awake for 15 days in a sealed chamber. According to the fictional narrative, the subjects descended into madness and self-mutilation. Despite being completely fabricated, the story has been widely shared and is frequently mistaken for genuine historical documentation. The creepypasta was first posted to the Creepypasta Wiki around 2010, with the original author remaining unknown. It has become a cornerstone of internet horror fiction and demonstrates the power of digital storytelling to create believable fictional narratives.

history.modern_era: The Russian Sleep Experiment remains one of the most recognized creepypastas. It has inspired fan art, short films, analysis videos, and academic discussion of internet folklore. The story serves as a case study in how digital narratives can blur the line between fiction and perceived reality.

Creepypasta community has always labeled it as fiction.
